ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT, as amended by Law No. 70 of 30 December 2019, Cabinet Decree No. 263 of 13 May 2021 and Cabinet Decree No. 233 of 29 November 2022; Executive Decree No. 158 of 2 June 2021 (Beneficial Ownership Registry and UBO declaration obligations); Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended; Decree-Law No. 2 of 23 February 2018 (Financial Analysis Unit framework); applicable resolutions and guidance issued by the UAF and the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct registration with the Registro Público de Panamá; no apostille or consular legalization required when executed before a Panamanian notary. If executed before a foreign notary, the charter requires a Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Hague jurisdictions).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction, or Consular Legalization at a Panamanian consulate for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled copy of passport of each founder, foundation council member, protector, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or residence of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted to the Panamanian resident agent for pre-incorporation filings and registry procedures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution, or Panamanian consular officer abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions; must be notarized and, where applicable, translated into Spanish.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, foundation council members, protectors, settlors, and beneficial owners against the Listado de Personas Designadas maintained by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN and other OFAC sanctions lists, EU restrictive measures, and additional global sanctions lists, with enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in Law 23 of 2015, and ongoing monitoring throughout the foundation's lifetime. Sanctions screening must be documented in the resident agent's KYC file and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá online services portal ('Servicios en Línea', www.registropublico.gob.pa), denomination search module and request for Certificate of Social Denomination (Certificado de Denominación Social)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be expressed in Latin script for inscription in the Panamanian Public Registry; the certificate is issued in Spanish. International and English-language names are accepted if transliterated into Latin characters, but the denomination must be sufficiently distinguishable and must include an operative term such as 'Fundación de Interés Privado', 'Fundación', or 'Private Interest Foundation' to evidence the foundation's legal nature.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley No. 13 de 16 de mayo de 2016; applicable sections include Articles 7, 12, 13, 15, 19-21, 25 and 36.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Notarial Charter Deed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: At least USD 10,000 (or equivalent in-kind assets) of founding assets; no escrow account required; the initial endowment must be fixed in the Foundation Charter and may be increased subsequently.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-forma First Resolution of the Foundation Council and Founder: (1) The founder subscribes an initial endowment of USD 10,000, which is irrevocably assigned to the Foundation and forms its patrimony. (2) The registered office is adopted at [Registered Office Address], Republic of Panama, and [Law Firm] is appointed as legal representative and registered agent. (3) [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed as members of the Foundation Council; [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] as Protector, each serving until removal in accordance with the Charter. (4) The President and Secretary are jointly authorized to execute registration filings, pay registry fees, open bank accounts, and obtain the Certificate of Registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Panamanian Registered Agent and Obtain Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent licensed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades y Fondos de Panamá (or an active Panamanian attorney listed by Registro Público)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a professional services engagement letter with a Panamanian law firm or licensed registered agent. Provide certified passport copies of the founder and foundation council members. The registered agent will conduct a name search with Registro Público and reserve the desired foundation name for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter signed by the founder
Certified passport copy of the founder
Certified passport copies of the proposed foundation council members
Brief statement of foundation purpose and beneficiary identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or confused with an existing entity, submit an alternative name reservation within 2 business days; the registered agent will expedite a corrected certificate of reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified Panamanian notary public in coordination with the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Spanish-language Escritura Pública de Constitución containing founder details, foundation name, purpose, initial endowment, registered office, foundation council composition, protector, beneficiary rules, bookkeeping provisions, amendment and dissolution procedures. Review and approve the draft with the registered agent and notary.
required_dossiers: Approved draft foundation charter
Name reservation certificate
Founder's written instructions regarding council members, protector, and beneficiaries
Anti-money-laundering client intake form (KYC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registered agent requests clarifications, circulate a legal memorandum and execute a revised draft; any legally defective clause is redrafted and re-notarized without restarting the entire process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá (Circuit jurisdiction where the registered office is located)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange physical or electronic appearance before the Panamanian notary public. The founder or the registered agent as attorney-in-fact executes the Escritura Pública, attesting to the lawful creation of the Private Interest Foundation. Pay notarial fees and obtain the notarized protocol copy.
required_dossiers: Final approved foundation charter
Original name reservation certificate
Identification documents of appearing parties
Proof of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies an irregularity in identification documents, obtain apostilled/certified copies from the relevant foreign authority and resubmit within 5 business days; no new name reservation is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Escritura Pública, together with a completed registration form and the registered agent's cover letter, to the Registry's filing window. Pay the official registry fee and obtain a stamped receipt. The Registry evaluates the deed for conformity with the Private Interest Foundation Law and issues the registered certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized protocol copy of the Escritura Pública
Completed Registro Público application form (Form/request signed by registered agent)
Receipt of payment of notarial fees
Registered agent's certification of good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a 'requerimiento' (query), respond in writing within 15 working days, filing a notarized corrective addendum or clarifying explanatory memorandum through the registered agent; expedited processing is available upon payment of an additional official fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Registration and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and the chosen private/business bank in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the final Certificate of Foundation Registration ('Cédula de Fundación') and the registry excerpts. Obtain a Panama tax identification number (RUC) for the foundation if it will hold a Panama business license. Open the corporate banking account with the registered agent's assistance; present the certificate, foundation charter, council resolution, and KYC documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Foundation Registration
Registry excerpt showing the foundation's public record
Foundation council resolution appointing signatories
Passport copies and bank references of officers/signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership evidence, provide a notarized foundation council resolution confirming underlying beneficiaries and a letter of reference; if a bank refuses, present the dossier to another licensed Panama bank through the registered agent's introductions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas; Municipality of the industrial location for Aviso de Operación
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso/Aviso de Operación Industrial de Manufactura de Plásticos (Industrial Operation Permit for Plastic Manufacturing)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Regular Environmental Registration (Ficha de Registro Ambiental) with a preliminary environmental impact statement; full EIA Report is not required for double-shot PBT plastic injection, unless production capacity exceeds 500 kg/day or involves hazardous chemical storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panama's Executive Decrees and MiAMBIENTE technical norms: treated wastewater discharges meeting maximum parameters for pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 150 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L; VOCs emitted from plastic injection and purging processes must be controlled by local exhaust ventilation and stack filters limiting annual VOC release to under 2 tonnes per source; plastic waste and off-spec keycaps must be segregated, stored under cover, and delivered to licensed recyclers or authorized disposal facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire safety certification and periodic inspections; structural load inspection carried out by a licensed civil engineer and filed with the municipal building office; workplace occupational clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), including noise control, machine guarding, ventilation, ergonomic, and occupational health assessments for injection molding operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Official e-services portal: www.dgi.gob.pa; electronic filing through 'E-Tax 2.0' / SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Tributación en Línea). Customs interface for export declarations: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA). Foundation registry interface: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Law 25 of 1995 or Law 70 of 2017 through a licensed Panamanian attorney; register the foundation charter (acta constitutiva) with the Registro Público de Panamá and obtain the nonexistence certificate ('certificado de no ser contribuyente') or direct RUC application. 2) Obtain the legal person's RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from the DGI by filing Form RUC-01, appointing a resident agent and, where applicable, a resident fiscal representative; foreign principals must provide an apostilled/legalized power of attorney and Spanish translation. 3) Apply for and activate the electronic signature (Firma Electrónica) issued through the Autoridad Nacional para la Innovación Gubernamental (AIG) to access the SITIO/E-Tax platform. 4) Register with the DGI as an ITBMS taxpayer when any taxable activity or export is performed; no de minimis exemption exists for registration, although small-turnover taxpayers may join the simplified small-taxpayer regime below B/.36,000 annual turnover. 5) Enroll with the MICI/VICOMEX National Exporters' Registry (Registro de Exportadores) before the first customs shipment. 6) Obtain a municipal Aviso de Operación/Patente Municipal only if the PIF maintains a fixed commercial establishment in Panama; an offshore/export-trading PIF without Panamanian premises is not required to obtain a municipal license. 7) Pay the annual PIF flat tax of B/.300 (USD 300 at parity) to the National Treasury via the Registro Público during the first quarter of each year and file the beneficial-ownership declaration with the DGI under Law 254 of 2021 (Beneficial Ownership Registry).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope. The PIF is a separate juridical person and is not a pass-through entity for Panamanian income tax. It is subject to entity-level income tax (ISR) at 25% exclusively on Panama-source income under Código Fiscal Article 694 et seq.; all foreign-source income, including export-trading profits with legal title transferred and economic control exercised outside Panama, is exempt from ISR with no remittance restriction. ITBMS applies only to Panamanian taxable supplies; properly documented physical exports are zero-rated (0%) with entitlement to input VAT credit refunds. Distributions of foreign income by the PIF to beneficiaries are not treated as dividends and are not subject to Panamanian withholding tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a 'check-the-box' or hybrid-mismatch election. The PIF is statutorily classified as a taxable juridical person, and no pass-through election is available for income tax. Relevant statutory elections: (i) election to be taxed under the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime where annual gross turnover does not exceed B/.36,000; (ii) election under the CAIR (Cálculo Alterno de Impuesto sobre la Renta) alternative minimum tax computation where applicable; (iii) for Panamanian corporations, the election to pay the 2% complementary/accumulated tax on taxable income to reduce the dividend withholding rate from 10% to 5% — not available for PIF distributions, which are not classifiable as dividends; (iv) election under Law 70 of 2017 to use the accelerated PIF incorporation procedure. No election can override Panama's territorial source-of-income rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a central bank; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) supervises banking, financial, and trust activities, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance coordinates monetary and financial policy within a fully dollarized legal framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The US dollar is legal tender and circulates freely alongside the national balboa (parity basis). No external exchange controls exist; both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible without central-bank approval. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation by a Private Interest Foundation are unrestricted from an FX perspective. Panama's territorial tax system does not impose a withholding tax or FX permit requirement on outbound profit remittances originating from foreign-source income; only Panamanian-source income may attract withholding, depending on the nature of the distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Panama. Exporters retain free disposition over foreign currency receipts, and no timeline is imposed for repatriation or conversion. The absence of a central bank means that no enforced FX settlement regime applies to proceeds from cross-border e-commerce sales.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with USD settlement and merchant acquiring capability
Operational Account / Multi-purpose collateral and escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex, or Currenxie may accept a Panama Private Interest Foundation on a case-by-case basis, but their legal status is not a regulated Panamanian financial institution. Such accounts cannot directly clear against Panama's local ACH (Sistema Clave) and generally rely on a tier-one bank sponsor. Feasibility is rated Medium for secondary receivables consolidation; primary treasury balances and supplier disbursements should be settled through a licensed Panamanian commercial bank to maintain full local enforceability and audit continuity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is strongly expected for first-time PIF account openings. At least one member of the Foundation Council or the designated registered agent must appear before the bank's compliance officer or a duly credentialed intermediary. Remote interviews via secure video are tolerated by private commercial banks only after a preliminary relationship, yet the final KYC sign-off generally requires a physical meeting, an apostilled foundation documentation packet, and verification of the founder's identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank de-risking of a Private Interest Foundation treated as a custodial or asset-holding vehicle with unclear economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Foundation Charter and Bylaws; DICR-E public registration certificate; sworn statutory purpose declaration restricted to legitimate e-commerce; documented economic substance in Duplicate or other operational records; a current Shopify/Stripe merchant account statement; bank references for directors or founders; and a source-of-wealth statement for the initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value inbound cross-border payments from payment processors creating a perceived retail money-laundering typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business dossier including product catalogue, factory purchase orders from the Chinese injection-molding supplier, commercial invoices, shipping and customs entries, warehouse lease, order-management dashboard export, and reconciliation of Stripe/Shopify settled amounts against inventory and logistics records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity because the founder is not an authorized Bank Signatory and is not physically present in Panama.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO disclosure form; passport and residence address verification of the founder; notarized written consent of the founder to the financial management arrangement; a Foundation Council resolution appointing the bank signatory; and a private-retained registered agent certificate confirming current legal representation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial founding capital is routed through a standard SWIFT MT103 wire from the founder's personal or corporate account to the PIF's principal operating account. The remittance field must state 'Business capital injection / capital contribution' and quote the foundation's name and account number. Receiving banks will typically require a copy of the incoming instruction, a source-of-funds breakdown, and a credit confirmation statement. Since Panama is fully dollarized, when wire origin is in a foreign currency the receiving bank will execute a spot FX trade at its own desk, with no restriction on the resulting USD balances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine settlement to foreign suppliers (e.g., PBT plastic pellet vendors, keycap mold shops, printing and packaging partners) is performed by SWIFT MT103 wire transfers denominated in USD or converted to CNY/EUR, with for high initial molds and first orders a Commercial Letter of Credit via the Panamanian bank confirmed by a Chinese correspondent bank. Recurring production runs after visual inspection can be paid through T/T (MT103), and all documentation including signed invoices, packing lists, bills of lading/airway bills, and bank settlement advices must be retained to evidence the genuine trade flow.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNY deliverable currency forwards via private banks for known supplier receivables
USD/EUR FX forwards for European customer settlement
Cross-currency FX swaps for matching of token-asset liquidity and supplier payables
USD/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) permitted through internationals banks acting as brokers, subject to bank counterparty due diligence
OTC FX options and interest-rate swaps entered under ISDA/ICC documentation and reported to the SBP-regulated counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Registry Tax (Annual Franchise Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; compliance status recorded by the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 2 January and 30 April for the calendar-year compliance cycle; for the 2025 cycle payment must be cleared by 30 April 2025
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory interest and penalties; a PIF with unpaid annual tax for two consecutive periods is placed on the Registro Público default list and, if not regularized, may be administratively struck off. While in default the foundation cannot obtain Registry certificates, solvency documents, or notarized formalities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) — required only if the PIF derives taxable Panama-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers must file within the DGI-published annual tax calendar; absent an administrative extension the return is due on or before 31 March following the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment expose the PIF to statutory surcharge, interest, and potential official estimated assessment by DGI; persistent non-filing may suspend tax-solvency certificates and restrict legal acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner / KYC Confidential Confirmation and Refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent; retained for inspection by the Dirección Nacional de Inteligencia Financiera (Panama Financial Intelligence Unit) under Law 23 of 2015
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every 12 months on the resident agent's review cycle; immediate refresh upon any change in foundation council, protector, beneficiary, or founder's dispositions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient UBO/KYC documentation may subject the PIF and the resident agent to monetary fines and regulatory sanctions; sustained non-compliant standing may contribute to Registry suspension or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Renewal / Compliance Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent and Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in line with the PIF's registration anniversary or the service-agreement renewal date; customarily aligned with the 30 April franchise-tax deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident agent and registered office in Panama constitutes a registrable default; the Public Registry may refuse to process documents and may proceed with administrative dissolution or strike-off of the foundation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Panama does not impose a blanket statutory audit obligation on passive Private Interest Foundations. An independent certified audit is triggered only where the PIF carries on economic activity in Panama and meets the DGI/MEF audit threshold for mandatory audited financial statements, or where the foundation charter, protector, or a regulatory request expressly requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; small and medium-sized entities may apply IFRS for SMEs. A passive PIF may maintain internal asset records without preparing statutory IFRS financial statements, unless the foundation deed or DGI obligations require otherwise.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Panama Private Interest Foundation has no shareholders and no share-transfer mechanism; founder's economic rights and beneficiary designations are changed by notarized private amendment or new foundation regulation. The resident agent must keep a confidential UBO/KYC file, perform an annual refresh within every 12-month cycle, and update that file immediately after any change in the founder, protector, Foundation Council, or beneficiaries. No public UBO declaration is filed with the Registro Público.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Notarized Foundation Charter and any private foundation regulations
Foundation Council Minute Book (Libro de Actas)
Resident Agent's Confidential UBO/KYC Register of beneficiaries, protectors, and council members

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a passive PIF; USD 2,500–6,000 if a DGI-required or deed-required certified audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate on net Panamanian-source profits of a licensed commercial entity. Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) are not per se exempt from corporate income tax; they are taxed only on income from Panamanian-source activities, consistent with Panama's territorial tax model. A purely passive PIF deriving foreign-source income is generically outside the Panamanian income tax base.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama's territorial regime exempts foreign-source income. Additional incentives include: (i) 100% exemption for income from eligible foreign export services, (ii) reduced taxation for qualified call-center and digital-service operators under special economic development laws, (iii) Colon Free Trade Zone and Ciudad del Saber preferential regimes, (iv) accelerated depreciation, (v) net operating loss carryforwards. A PIF's passive income from non-Panamanian sources is not subject to Panamanian corporate tax. A custom mechanical keyboard keycap operation selling via foreign payment rails would normally be outside Panama-source taxation unless local manufacturing, warehousing, or sales activity occurs within Panamanian territory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta Personas Jurídicas) filed through Panama's DGI e-filing system, 'eVentanilla' (Ventanilla Electrónica de la DGI) using taxpayer RUC registration. The form is the statutory annual income tax return for Panamanian legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations when they derive Panamanian-source income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. In addition to the annual CIT return, larger taxpayers may be required to make quarterly advance income tax payments (Pagos Provisionales) for the current fiscal period. For most calendar-year entities, the annual CIT return is due no later than March 15 of the following year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end. For taxpayers on a January 1 to December 31 fiscal year, the filing deadline is March 15 of the immediately succeeding calendar year. DGI may grant extensions only through prior request and only for a period not exceeding 30 days, subject to advance tax deposit requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the full Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) tax identification number, entity legal name registered with the Public Registry, and the fiscal period start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF with Panamanian-source taxable activities must already have a resident agent, an active RUC, and a Panama fiscal domicile. Enter the RUC exactly as shown on the DGI registration certificate. If no Panamanian-source income exists, check the 'semilla' or 'non-commercial operation' box in the corresponding operating-status field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all gross revenue, gains, and income attributed to Panamanian territorial source, including sales of keycaps delivered or manufactured in Panama, local e-commerce warehouse services, and locally performed services. Include all invoiced amounts before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foundations should only record amounts attributable to Panamanian source. Income from sales of custom mechanical keyboard caps to customers abroad through Shopify Payments or Stripe, with all fulfillment outside Panama, should be classified as foreign-source and excluded from Box 3.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare income from sources outside Panama. For a PIF engaged in the distribution of keyboard keycaps using non-Panamanian manufacturing and logistics, all foreign-sourced profit is reported as exempt under the territorial income tax system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF must complete Box 4 if it maintains accounting records of foreign-source receipts. Panama does not tax these amounts; however, the declarant must maintain contemporaneous invoices, shipping documents, and foreign bank records demonstrating the offshore sourcing and the absence of Panamanian economic activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter directly attributable costs, expenses, depreciation, and deductions sustained for Panamanian-source income. Only expenses causally connected to the taxable Panamanian income are deductible. Allocation rules require a proportional cost-sharing methodology when mixed-source income exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foundations should not offset foreign operating expenses against Panamanian-source income unless the expenses are directly connected to that Panamanian business. Maintain separate cost ledgers for Panama-sourced sales and offshore sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income equals Panama-source gross revenues minus allowable Panamanian deductions and exemptions. The result is the tax base subject to the 25% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident foundations reporting zero Panama-source taxable activity, enter zero. A PIF deriving only foreign-source income is not required to compute net taxable income under Panamanian law, but full supporting schedules should remain available to the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the standard 25% corporate income tax rate to the net taxable income in Box 6. Do not include complementary dividend withholding here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities using the territorial exemption do not apply the 25% rate to foreign-source profit. If a treaty-protected permanent establishment exists, apply the relevant DTA assignment rules as transposed by Panamanian regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the product of Box 6 and Box 7, plus any alternative minimum tax if the taxpayer is subject to the IMAN (Impuesto Mínimo Alterno) for large taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs are generally not subject to IMAN if their only business activity is passive foreign-source trade. If the DGI has assessed a minimum tax based on gross assets, attach evidence of the off-shore asset holding structure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List advanced income tax payments (pagos provisionales), withholding tax credits, and any creditable taxes withheld by Panamanian customers or payment processors during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign PIFs with no Panama-source income may have zero advance payments. If local withholding occurred on Panamanian-source sales, enter that amount and attach the corresponding electronic receipts from the withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Annual Franchise Tax and DGI Surcharge Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the annual legal entity franchise tax (commonly USD 300 for private foundations) with the income tax declaration. This field captures the relationship of paid franchise taxes to the DGI record.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Private Interest Foundations must pay their annual franchise tax separately through the Public Registry or designated banks. Verify that the Foundation Law 25 annual fee has been paid before submitting Form 110 to avoid blocking of the filing acknowledgment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex TP - Related Party Transaction Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach a transfer pricing declaration if the PIF or its commercial subsidiary has related-party cross-border transactions above the statutory documentation threshold. The form must include the counterparty, legal relationship, controlled transaction category, amount, and transfer pricing method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foundations transacting with an affiliated keycap manufacturer or logistics provider in another jurisdiction must present a contemporaneous benchmarking or TP documentation file when the threshold is triggered, even if each related-party transaction is with a foreign entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under the Panama Tax Code range from USD 50 to USD 5,000 per unfiled return, depending on the taxpayer's income tier. Additionally, unpaid tax liabilities accrue default interest of 10% per year (or 1% per month), and late payment surcharges may rise to 10% of the outstanding tax. Failure to file for three consecutive periods can result in administrative cancellation of the RUC, prohibition of banking transactions, and no issuance of the 'Paz y Salvo' tax clearance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends or profit distributions paid out of Panama-source taxable profits. Panamanian private interest foundation distributions to beneficiaries are generally treated as dispositions of foundation assets rather than taxable dividends when the underlying assets are not derived from Panamanian commercial activity. Where a PIF does distribute Panamanian business earnings, the 10% dividend withholding tax is required, payable with the corporate income tax return through the corresponding Form 198 (Declaración Mensual de Dividendos) and annual reconciliation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a limited but effective double tax treaty (DTA) network. Beneficiary residents of treaty jurisdictions (e.g., Mexico, Netherlands, Qatar, Singapore, Spain, South Korea, and the United Arab Emirates) may apply for reduced dividend withholding rates. The administrative protocol is: (i) obtain a Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) from the jurisdiction's tax authority, (ii) provide a signed beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is not an intermediary, (iii) submit the TRC and support to the Panamanian withholding agent or DGI before the dividend payment, (iv) complete the applicable DGI e-form applying the reduced treaty rate or exemption, and (v) retain all documents for at least seven years. In practice, the Panamanian withholding agent must eff ectively assess the DTA benefit; if the form cannot be filed in advance, the recipient may request a refund from the DGI after withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding rates: royalties for use of trademarks, patents, and other industrial intellectual property in Panama are subject to a 12.5% gross-basis withholding tax when the payment is Panama-source. Interest payments to non-resident financial institutions from offshore loans are generally outside Panamanian source taxation; however, interest arising from Panamanian-source debts or paid by a Panamanian permanent establishment is subject to withholding at 25% on the gross interest, unless reduced by a DTA. A PIF engaged in inbound licensing of keyboard keycap mold designs and injection technology must monitor both the beneficial ownership residence and the place of use. Treaty relief may reduce royalty withholding to 5%-10% and interest withholding under the applicable DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 2,500,000 (two million five hundred thousand Panamanian Balboas, at parity with USD) in annual gross income. Panamanian tax regulations require entities above this threshold to prepare and submit transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File contours) with their annual CIT return when they execute cross-border controlled transactions. For lower-income taxpayers, contemporaneous TP documentation should still be maintained if related-party transactions are material, but statutory Local/Master File filing obligations are triggered by this gross income threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities licensed or registered in Panama carrying on relevant activities, including distribution and service center activity, financing, leasing, headquarters, holding, intellectual property holding, and shipping. A PIF that merely owns a custom keyboard keycap brand or IP and receives royalties without local management and physical operations may be challenged as lacking economic substance. ESR compliance generally requires: (i) full board and management control exercised in Panama, (ii) adequate local premises proportionate to the activity, (iii) qualified local staff, and (iv) operational spending in Panama. A PIF deriving only foreign-origin trading income through non-Panama supply chains should maintain an ESR file demonstrating why it is not tax resident in Panama or why the Panamanian relevant activity is not carried out. The absence of substantive business activity, combined with the use of personal liability foundations, exposes the structure to substance-based audits and exchange-of-information disclosures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Panamanian Corporate Income Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panamanian-source sales from Box 3 of Form 110, including concealed local e-commerce sales or unrecorded revenue derived from domestic inventory held in Panama; artificially classifying domestic keycap manufacturing operations as 'foreign-source'; using a PIF as a sham to cover a real Panamanian commercial business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion is punishable with a fine of up to ten times the evaded tax and penal imprisonment. Administrative re-assessment carries a 25% surcharge plus default interest at 10% per annum. The DGI may also suspend the RUC and revoke existing tax clearance certificates, freezing the entity's ability to receive payment funds through local PSPs or banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian courts have upheld lifting the foundation/corporate veil where the foundation was an instrument of tax evasion. Directors, resident agents, and effective beneficial owners may be held jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, subject to travel bans, asset seizures, and imprisonment of up to 5 years for fraudulent concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A PIF holding a high-value custom keyboard caps trademark or e-commerce enterprise without physical substance, local office, independent governance, or active decision-making; no evidence of economic activity in Panama despite claiming Panamanian tax residence; operating purely as a mailbox entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's economic substance enforcement framework and anti-money laundering rules, non-compliant entities may be subjected to fines from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000; cancellation of the registration and the foundation charter; loss of access to the tax exemption for foreign-source income; and mandatory revocation of the resident agent license where the agent knowingly assisted in the sham arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and resident agents who sign false declarations can be fined up to USD 500,000 and disqualified from serving in Panama for 10 years. In serious cases, civil restitution claims may be brought by the DGI against the director's personal estate, and corresponding travel restrictions are issued to prevent flight.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / AML Red Flags on Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panama Private Interest Foundation to operate a Shopify / Stripe account with undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners; collecting customer payments under a false trade description; mixing third-party merchants' funds; accepting unexplained wire transfers from high-risk jurisdictions or shell bank accounts; failing to register or report the foundation's foundation council and beneficiary identity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's AML Law 23 of 2015 and subsequent reforms impose administrative fines of up to USD 5,000,000 for seriously impaired AML controls. Criminal penalties for organized crime or money laundering include 5 to 12 years imprisonment. The AML supervisor (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá) may order immediate freezing of the relevant accounts and termination of PSP agreements with Shopify Payments or Stripe processing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members (directors) and appointed compliance officers are personally liable for failing to maintain adequate records of the beneficial owner. The penalty extends to imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for false documentation and the assessment of civil damages against the personal estate of the director for facilitating the money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misdeclaration and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file transfer pricing documentation when the PIF's commercial trading arm exceeds the B/. 2,500,000 threshold; pricing keycap purchase and resale margins to offshore affiliates without an arm's length benchmark; shifting profit through royalty payments to tax haven related entities; failing to retain comparable data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with transfer pricing documentation triggers a penalty of 5% of the value of the controlled transactions, with a maximum penalty of USD 100,000. If the DGI makes a primary transfer pricing adjustment, a 20% surcharge on the additional tax due plus interest accrues. Persistent non-compliance can result in double counting of penalties and loss of territorial exemptions for the underlying transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign and approve false transfer pricing reports may be personally assessed for 50% of the penalty when they were conscious of the misstatement. In aggravated cases, they are exposed to criminal tax liability under Article 51 of the Panama Criminal Code and may suffer personal bankruptcy orders, travel bans, and restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Franchise Tax and Statutory Filing Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-payment of the annual Panama Private Interest Foundation franchise tax (currently USD 300); failure to file the annual Form 110 return; failure to update the RUC or resident agent information; failure to submit the annual foundation council minutes required by the Public Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Public Registry may impose late fines for foundation annual fee defaults, and after repeated non-payment, the foundation's legal status is suspended, rendering the PIF unable to execute contracts or maintain bank and payment processing accounts. DGI penalties for late Form 110 filing range from USD 50 to USD 5,000, plus default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council members are under a fiduciary duty to ensure the annual fee is Paid. If the foundation's insolvency or non-compliance damages a beneficiary, the council members and resident agent can be held personally liable for restitution under Foundation Law 25 of 1995, including claims for improper distribution and breach of fiduciary obligations, with courts able to issue personal asset freezes.
